_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the guinea-pig crossing watch schedules.
Every table in docs/ that names a time, an owner or a trigger is GENERATED
from this file by scripts/render-crossing-schedule.mjs. Do not hand-edit those
tables — `pnpm check:schedule` fails if they drift from this file.
WHY: on 2026-09-16 four documents restated this schedule and gave three
different answers. Two operational pages said 'Fatih primary, Rakha backup',
which was the inverse of what had been agreed in #104. A summary table and the
sections it summarises drift apart when only one is edited, and the table is
what people read on the day.
WATCHES, added 2026-09-22. This file held ONE subject and all four of B's
checkpoints were in the past, so five operational pages were rendering a table
for a finished event four days before the one that had not happened. The check
stayed green throughout: it verifies the tables match this file, never that
this file matches the calendar. The renderer now selects the first watch whose
status is 'upcoming' and names the completed ones above it.
EACH SUBJECT HAS TWO DATES and they are one day apart. crossesAtUtc is the
ALERT THRESHOLD; expiresAtUtc is the EXPIRY, which is the unrepeatable event.
write-guard.ts owns both as alertThresholdOn and expiresOn.

watches.completedNote: All four slots captured; every bundle verifies. Slot 4 has one bundle rather than two — the secondary machine slept through the expiry window. Decay measured: 17,279 → 8,641 → 4,319 → expired. See docs/W3-B-WATCH-CLOSING.md.

checkpoints.note: Declined once as part of the 01:00/07:00 WIB pair, then accepted as a standalone 07:00 WIB morning slot after 01:00 was dropped.
Accepted on first asking. It is the slot that fills the twelve-hour gap running into expiry.

declined.reason: Not for want of a volunteer — it is the wrong place for a checkpoint. It would have made the sequence dense early and left a twelve-hour gap running into expiry, which is the interval a reader actually asks about. The 06:00 UTC slot fills that gap instead, and costs a lunchtime rather than a night.

checkpoints.note: Same shape as B's slot 1. Nobody has accepted it yet.
07:00 WIB. B's equivalent slot was accepted as a standalone morning slot.
Fills the twelve-hour gap running into expiry, which is the interval a reader asks about.

checkpoints.what: EXPIRY — Saturday, happens once, nothing comes after it
checkpoints.note: A WEEKEND SLOT, against the weekends-are-not-working-days assumption. B's expiry produced only one bundle because the secondary machine slept; this is the last chance at two. Assessment needs a ledger above the PERSISTENT entry's 4,880,099, not the instance's 4,880,097.
